title: The Demo I Wish I'd Had: OpenAI's Agents SDK... serverless! - Brook Riggio
talk_summary: A tour of a preferred full-stack serverless agent stack (Next.js + OpenAI Agents SDK in Python + Inngest orchestration + Vercel hosting), demoed with a newsletter-generating app. The only substantive engineering content is Inngest's step-based durable workflow model and its retry/observability semantics.

takeaways.technique: Step-scoped durable workflow with per-step retries
takeaways.what_they_do: Each agent call is wrapped in a step.run so the orchestrator retries and resumes at step granularity, giving step-level observability and avoiding whole-run restarts.
takeaways.evidence_quote: every step.run will be invoked in order, but code that's outside of step.run ... may well be executed multiple times

takeaways.technique: Split long agent tasks into short independent functions
takeaways.what_they_do: Breaks the workflow into separate research and formatting agent endpoints so each runs as its own short-lived function within platform time limits.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Each one of those steps can scale up and down to the full length of what Verscell allows for a cloud function to run.

takeaways.technique: Event-triggered orchestration instead of always-on workers
takeaways.what_they_do: Uses event triggers to start workflows on demand, avoiding idle warm servers and paying only for execution.
takeaways.evidence_quote: It's you don't have to manage JSON documents of state machines ... it works entirely on demand.

takeaways.what_they_do: Every push gets an isolated preview URL so the team reviews the running change before merge.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Verscell's got preview deployments with every push.
